findings.description: This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses to instances launched in it and is associated with a route table with a default route to an internet gateway. This creates unnecessary direct internet exposure for future workloads placed in the subnet.

This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with an internet-gateway default route. The portal_server is deployed here, making the security group's public ingress rules reachable from the internet.
The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption. Its contents can be stored unencrypted unless an account-level default outside this configuration is enabled.

User data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These credentials are exposed in infrastructure configuration and may be obtainable via instance user-data access, enabling use of the associated IAM principal's permissions.
TCP port 22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. The attached portal_server has a public IP in an internet-routed subnet, exposing SSH to all internet hosts.

The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration in this Terraform. Although S3 applies baseline SSE-S3 encryption by default for new uploads, this configuration does not explicitly enforce an encryption requirement or a customer-managed encryption policy for this security telemetry.
The snapshot is created from a volume that is not configured as encrypted, so the snapshot is likewise not assured to be encrypted at rest.
